mainTopic: Whether selling and slaughtering are linked for the four-or-five payment (רבי יוחנן vs. ריש לקיש), and why a stolen כלאים animal is included
overview: This amud finishes ריש לקיש's explanation of רבי שמעון: an animal that is ready to be redeemed is treated as if it were already redeemed. The גמרא then asks why ריש לקיש did not accept רבי יוחנן's approach. It answers with the פסוק 'וּטְבָחוֹ וּמְכָרוֹ', which ties slaughtering to selling. The two אמוראים follow the same views in another argument, about a thief who sells a stolen טריפה according to רבי שמעון. רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a ברייתא, and after some back-and-forth over how the ברייתא is worded, ריש לקיש is left with a קשיא. Then the גמרא asks why a thief pays four or five for a כלאים animal when the theft פסוק says שה. רבא explains that the word או includes כלאים in the theft פסוק but leaves it out in the קדשים פסוק, depending on which animals each פסוק lists.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the red heifer can be redeemed even on its pyre
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reports that רבי שמעון held a פרה אדומה can be redeemed with money even after it has been slaughtered on its pyre.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: רבי שמעון used to say that the red heifer can be redeemed even when it is already on its pyre.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש brings a statement of רבי שמעון to back up his own explanation of the משנה. It shows that, in רבי שמעון's view, a holy animal can be redeemed even very late in the process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש explained the משנה as speaking about blemished קדשים, which can be redeemed and then eaten. Here he shows that רבי שמעון takes redemption very far: even a פרה אדומה already slaughtered on its pyre can still be redeemed. This supports treating the slaughter as 'fit', because the animal could still become permitted through פדיון.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer, burned to make ashes for purification
Can be redeemed (its holiness moved onto money)
Its pyre, the arranged pile of wood it is burned on
He used to say

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said,
Rabbi Shimon used to say:
The heifer can be redeemed
phrases.notes: This is the פרה אדומה, the red heifer.

phrases.english: on top of its pyre.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ריש לקיש's explanation of רבי שמעון from just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, a פרה אדומה can be redeemed even after slaughter, on its pyre.

steps.title: Anything ready to be redeemed counts as redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the rule from רבי שמעון: anything that stands ready to be redeemed is treated as if it were already redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that anything that is ready to be redeemed is considered as if it were already redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls a general rule out of the statement about the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the animal could be redeemed at any moment, רבי שמעון treats it as if it already were. That is why a blemished holy animal slaughtered by a thief counts as a 'fit' slaughter: it is as good as redeemed, and its meat could be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidently, so we see
Something that is ready to be redeemed
Is treated as already redeemed

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, כל העומד לפדות כפדוי דמי: what is ready to be redeemed is treated as redeemed. This is how ריש לקיש explains the משנה with blemished קדשים.

phrases.english: Evidently, anything that stands ready to be redeemed
is considered as if redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle from the פרה אדומה statement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי שמעון, anything ready to be redeemed is treated as already redeemed.

steps.title: Why didn't ריש לקיש accept רבי יוחנן's explanation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why רבי יוחנן rejected ריש לקיש's approach, but asks why ריש לקיש rejected רבי יוחנן's.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רבי יוחנן did not explain like ריש לקיש, because he wants the משנה to cover even unblemished animals. But why didn't ריש לקיש explain like רבי יוחנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two explanations of the משנה. It sets up a question that the next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's answer only works for blemished animals, so רבי יוחנן avoided it in order to read the משנה as covering unblemished animals too. רבי יוחנן's answer seems to work more broadly, so the גמרא asks what ריש לקיש found wrong with it.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that...
To explain it as dealing with a certain case
Unblemished animals
What is the reason?

phrases.english: It makes sense that Rabbi Yochanan did not say
like Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
because he wants to explain the Mishnah
as including even unblemished animals.
But Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say like Rabbi Yochanan?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both explanations are on the table, the גמרא asks why each אמורא avoided the other's approach.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did ריש לקיש find wrong with רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה?

steps.title: Slaughtering is tied to selling
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds that the פסוק links slaughtering to selling. Since selling קדשים is not a real sale, slaughtering them cannot bring the payment of ארבעה וחמשה either, unless they are blemished and redeemable.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: the verse says 'and slaughters it or sells it.' Wherever selling counts, slaughtering counts, and wherever selling does not count, slaughtering does not count. With holy animals, selling them is not a real sale, so slaughtering them does not count either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing ריש לקיש's source: the פסוק places slaughtering and selling side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק mentions them together, ריש לקיש treats them as one rule: a thief pays four or five times only where both would apply. Unblemished קדשים cannot be legally sold at all, so slaughtering them also cannot bring the payment. That is why ריש לקיש limits the משנה to blemished animals, which can be redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And slaughters it or sells it', the פסוק about a thief
Selling
Slaughtering
Holy animals set aside for sacrifices
Since

steps.whyThisMatters: This link between selling and slaughtering is the root of the disagreement between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן, and it comes up again in the next step.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
'And slaughters it or sells it':
anywhere that it applies to selling
it applies to slaughtering,
and anywhere that it does not apply to selling
it does not apply to slaughtering.
And these holy animals,
since when one sells holy animals
it is not a real sale,
slaughtering does not apply to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why ריש לקיש did not follow רבי יוחנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ties slaughtering to selling. Unblemished קדשים cannot be sold, so their slaughter cannot bring the payment of ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: Each follows his own view: selling a stolen טריפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are consistent. They also argue about a thief who sells a stolen טריפה according to רבי שמעון: רבי יוחנן says he is liable, ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: They follow their own reasoning, as it was stated: if someone sells a טריפה, according to רבי שמעון, רבי יוחנן says he is liable and ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a second argument between the same two אמוראים that matches what we just learned about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, slaughtering a טריפה is not a 'fit' slaughter, since it does not make the animal permitted to eat. ריש לקיש, who ties selling to slaughtering, says selling it is also exempt. רבי יוחנן does not tie them together this way, so a sale of a טריפה still brings the payment.

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own reasoning
As it was stated (a teaching of the אמוראים)
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
Liable / exempt

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש consistently ties selling to slaughtering: where one does not bring the payment of ארבעה וחמשה, the other does not either. רבי יוחנן does not hold this link.
steps.confusionAlert: Being 'liable' here means paying four or five times the value for selling the stolen animal, not just returning it or paying for it.

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning,
as it was stated:
One who sells a stolen tereifa,
according to the words of Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: This means: going by רבי שמעון's rule that a slaughter that is not fit does not count as slaughter.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: he is liable,
and Reish Lakish says: he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the selling-slaughtering link behind ריש לקיש's view also shapes another argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, a thief who sells a stolen טריפה is liable according to רבי יוחנן and exempt according to ריש לקיש.

steps.title: The reasoning behind each side
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the thief is liable, because selling counts even when slaughtering would not. ריש לקיש says he is exempt, because if slaughtering does not count, selling does not count either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he is liable: even though the payment does not apply to slaughtering a טריפה, it does apply to selling it. ריש לקיש says he is exempt: since it does not apply to slaughtering, it does not apply to selling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the reason behind each side of the argument about selling a stolen טריפה according to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, slaughtering a טריפה does not count, because the animal cannot be eaten anyway. רבי יוחנן treats selling as a separate act that can count on its own. ריש לקיש holds that the פסוק ties selling to slaughtering, so whatever does not count for one does not count for the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable, has to pay
Exempt, does not have to pay
Slaughtering
Selling
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even if slaughtered properly

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says selling can count on its own. ריש לקיש says selling and slaughtering always go together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: he is liable,
even though it does not apply to slaughtering,
phrases.notes: "It" means the payment of four and five. A טריפה's slaughter doesn't count here, because it can't be eaten anyway.

phrases.english: it does apply to selling.
And Reish Lakish says: he is exempt,
since it does not apply to slaughtering,
it does not apply to selling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the dispute that step 5 reported.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: selling can obligate even when slaughtering cannot. ריש לקיש: if slaughtering cannot obligate, selling cannot either.

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to back רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes a ברייתא: a thief who sells a stolen טריפה pays ארבעה וחמשה. He argues that it follows רבי שמעון, which would show that selling counts even when slaughtering does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: 'If one stole a כלאים animal and slaughtered it, or a טריפה and sold it, he pays four and five.' Isn't this רבי שמעון? So even though slaughtering does not count, selling does!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view with a ברייתא that seems to support his own position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists only selling for a טריפה, not slaughtering. That suggests slaughtering a טריפה would not count, which is רבי שמעון's view. So according to רבי שמעון, selling a טריפה still obligates the thief, which goes against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him from a source
A mixed-breed animal, such as a cross between a sheep and a goat
The fourfold or fivefold payment a thief pays for slaughtering or selling a stolen sheep or ox
"Isn't it...?": introduces the reading the questioner is proposing
So we see, apparently

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
If one stole a mixed-breed animal and slaughtered it,
or a tereifa and sold it,
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.
What, is it not Rabbi Shimon's view?

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵיתֵיהּ בִּטְבִיחָה –
phrases.english: So we see that even though it does not apply to slaughtering,
it does apply to selling!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's side of the dispute laid out in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that according to רבי שמעון, selling a טריפה does not obligate the thief.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists only selling for a טריפה, which suggests it follows רבי שמעון. Yet it still makes the thief pay for selling, so selling counts even when slaughtering does not.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the ברייתא follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the ברייתא does not follow רבי שמעון. It follows the רבנן, who disagree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No, it is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends his view by saying the ברייתא follows the רבנן, not רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא follows the רבנן, it says nothing about רבי שמעון's opinion. The proof against ריש לקיש falls away, because the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש is only about what רבי שמעון holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion that disagrees with רבי שמעון here

phrases.english: He said to him: No;
it follows the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The רבנן hold that slaughtering a טריפה also counts, even though it can't be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by assigning the ברייתא to a different opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון and shows that selling counts on its own.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the רבנן, so it proves nothing about רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Then why mention only selling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the רבנן hold that slaughtering a טריפה also counts. So why would the ברייתא mention only selling a טריפה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is the רבנן, does a טריפה count for selling but not for slaughtering?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's answer. Assigning the ברייתא to the רבנן doesn't fit how it is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, a thief pays for slaughtering a טריפה as well as for selling it. A ברייתא following them would have said 'a טריפה, and he slaughtered it.' Mentioning only selling makes sense only according to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: If
Slaughtering, another word for טְבִיחָה
It applies / it does not apply

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not that the רבנן exempt slaughtering a טריפה. They clearly make the thief pay for it. The question is why the ברייתא would leave that case out if it follows them.

phrases.english: If it follows the Rabbis,
does a tereifa count for selling
but not count for slaughtering?!
phrases.notes: He means: for the רבנן slaughtering counts too, so why would the ברייתא pick only selling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's answer in step 8 based on how the ברייתא is worded.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן make the thief pay for slaughtering a טריפה too, so a ברייתא following them would not single out selling. The wording fits only רבי שמעון.

steps.title: A counter-question: the same problem exists for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 9 with a question of its own. If the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, why does it mention only slaughtering for כלאים? Selling a כלאים animal surely counts too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what would you say instead, that it follows רבי שמעון?! Then would you say that for כלאים slaughtering counts but selling does not?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around. It shows that even if the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, the ברייתא still leaves something out in the כלאים case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the problem was that, according to the רבנן, the ברייתא mentions only selling for a טריפה. Here the גמרא points out that, according to רבי שמעון, the ברייתא mentions only slaughtering for כלאים, even though everyone agrees selling a כלאים animal also counts. So mentioning only one action cannot prove anything about who wrote the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather what? This opens a counter-question.
An animal born from two different species, such as a goat and a sheep.
Slaughtering
Selling

phrases.english: But rather what, [does it follow] רבי שמעון?!
For diverse kinds, [the payment] applies when it is slaughtered,
but does not apply when it is sold?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 with a counter-question that shows the same problem appears if the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון because it mentions only selling for the טריפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא also mentions only slaughtering for כלאים, and selling a כלאים animal certainly counts. So leaving out one action is no proof.

steps.title: The ברייתא mentions one action but means both
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the ברייתא states one action and means the other one as well. That same answer works for the רבנן: it says selling for the טריפה, and slaughtering counts too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it taught slaughtering, and the same is true for selling. Then say the same for the רבנן too: it taught selling, and the same is true for slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא sometimes names only one action while meaning both. It uses this to defend ריש לקיש's reading that the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, we already have to say that 'slaughtering' in the כלאים case also covers selling. Once we accept that, we can just as easily say that 'selling' in the טריפה case also covers slaughtering, which matches the רבנן. So the question from step 9 goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught. This refers to what the ברייתא stated.
And the same is true. The rule also applies to the other case.
Say

phrases.english: Rather, it taught slaughtering
and the same is true for selling;
say [the same] for the Rabbis as well:
it taught selling
and the same is true for slaughtering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תְּנָא טְבִיחָה וְהוּא הַדִּין לִמְכִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the counter-question and uses the same answer to defend ריש לקיש's reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording: naming one action stands for both.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the ברייתא mentions only selling for the טריפה, it must follow רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא names one action and means both, so it can follow the רבנן.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: for רבי שמעון the short wording has a reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rejects the comparison. According to רבי שמעון, the ברייתא had to teach the טריפה case only with selling. Because of that, it also taught the כלאים case with only one action, to keep the two cases matching.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן would tell you: What kind of comparison is this? It makes sense if you say the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. Since it taught the טריפה case in only one way, it taught the כלאים case in only one way too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers back and says the two cases are not alike. He explains why, according to רבי שמעון, it makes sense for the ברייתא to mention only one action in each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, slaughtering a טריפה does not count, so the ברייתא could only write selling for that case. Once it wrote the טריפה case with one action, it wrote the כלאים case with one action too, just to keep the style the same. So according to רבי שמעון, the short wording has a real cause.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? Meaning, this comparison does not work.
Granted, it makes sense if
Since; because it already did one thing, it did the other the same way.
In one way, with only one action

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you:
What is this [comparison]?
Granted, if you say [it follows] Rabbi Shimon,
since it taught tereifa in one [way],
phrases.notes: According to רבי שמעון, slaughtering a טריפה doesn't count, so the ברייתא could only write selling.

phrases.english: it taught diverse kinds in one [way].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר לָךְ הַאי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 11 by showing the two cases are not the same.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the כלאים case according to רבי שמעון and the טריפה case according to the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רבי שמעון the one-action wording has a reason, because the טריפה case could only be written with selling. According to the רבנן there is no such reason.

steps.title: For the רבנן the ברייתא should have combined both cases
steps.stepSummary: According to the רבנן, nothing would stop the ברייתא from joining the two cases: 'one who stole כלאים or a טריפה and slaughtered or sold them pays four or five.' The ברייתא did not write it that way, so ריש לקיש is left with a difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say it follows the רבנן, it should have combined them and taught them together: one who stole a כלאים animal or a טריפה and slaughtered or sold them pays the four-or-five payment! This is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes his argument. According to the רבנן, the ברייתא should have written one combined sentence. The גמרא ends with 'קשיא', which means ריש לקיש's reading is left with a difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, slaughtering and selling count the same way for both כלאים and טריפה. So there was no reason to split the cases, and the ברייתא should have written one combined sentence. The fact that it split them suggests it follows רבי שמעון, which supports רבי יוחנן that selling counts even when slaughtering would not.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it combine them and teach them together.
The four-or-five payment a thief pays for slaughtering or selling a stolen animal.
It is difficult. The question stays unanswered, but the opinion is not fully thrown out.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא wrote the טריפה case only with selling and the כלאים case only with slaughtering. That fits רבי שמעון, so it supports רבי יוחנן. ריש לקיש is left with a קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: קשיא is not the same as תיובתא. It means the difficulty stays unanswered, but ריש לקיש's opinion is not formally rejected.

phrases.english: But if you say [it follows] the Rabbis,
let it combine them and teach them [together]:
If one stole diverse kinds or a tereifa,
and slaughtered them or sold them,
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment!
It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ רַבָּנַן נְעָרְבִינְהוּ וְנִיתְנִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יוחנן's rejection and leaves ריש לקיש with a difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim in step 8 that the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the רבנן, the two cases follow the same rule, so the ברייתא should have combined them. Splitting them only makes sense according to רבי שמעון.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא is best read according to רבי שמעון, which supports רבי יוחנן. ריש לקיש is left with a קשיא.

steps.title: How can a mixed animal count when the Torah says 'שה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's ruling that stealing a כלאים animal brings the four-or-five payment. The theft פסוק says שה, and רבא taught that שה always leaves out כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כלאים animal? The פסוק says 'שה'! And רבא said: this פסוק sets a pattern. Wherever the Torah says 'שה', it comes to leave out כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions a different part of the ברייתא: the ruling that a thief pays four or five for a כלאים animal. It points to a rule from רבא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four-or-five payment comes from the פסוק 'If a man steals an ox or a שה.' רבא learned from a פסוק in דברים that the word שה means a real sheep or a real goat, not a mix of the two. So a כלאים animal should not be covered by this פסוק at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, an animal born from a mix of two species, like a sheep and a goat
A sheep or a goat
Built a pattern; one פסוק sets a rule that applies to other places
To leave out (exclude)

phrases.english: A כלאים animal? 'Seh' is written!
And רבא said: this verse sets a pattern:
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק about which animals you may eat, דברים 14:4.

phrases.english: Wherever 'seh' is said,
it comes only to leave out the mixed animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבנן/רבי שמעון discussion and opens a new question on the ברייתא's כלאים ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a thief pays four or five for a כלאים animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The theft פסוק says שה, and רבא's rule says שה always leaves out כלאים. So כלאים should not be covered.

steps.title: The extra word 'or' adds the mixed animal back in
steps.stepSummary: The theft פסוק is different. It uses the word או ('or'), and that word comes to include כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because the פסוק says 'או', and that comes to include כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. In the theft פסוק, the word 'or' adds the כלאים animal back in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule about שה still stands. But the theft פסוק has an extra word, או, and an extra word teaches something more. Here it brings back the כלאים animal that שה would have left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different
The פסוק
To include, to add something in

phrases.english: Here it is different, because the verse says 'or':
phrases.notes: The theft פסוק says 'an ox or a שה'.

phrases.english: to include the mixed animal.

steps.terutzResolutionType: An extra word in this פסוק overrides the usual rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שה always leaves out כלאים, so the theft payment should not apply to it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra או in the theft פסוק adds כלאים back in.

steps.title: But in the offerings verse, 'or' leaves the mixed animal out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether או always includes. A ברייתא about קדשים uses או to leave out כלאים and a נדמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does every 'או' come to include? But a ברייתא teaches: 'An ox or a sheep' leaves out כלאים. 'Or a goat' leaves out a look-alike animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 15. In another פסוק, about offerings, the same word 'or' is used to leave animals out, not to add them in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said that או includes כלאים. But in the קדשים ברייתא, the 'or' in 'an ox or a sheep' is read as leaving out כלאים. So how can the same word do opposite jobs?

keyTerms.meaning: But a ברייתא teaches (introduces a source that seems to argue)
To exclude, to leave out
A look-alike: an animal born of one species that looks like another

phrases.english: And is every 'or' meant to include?
But it was taught: 'An ox or a sheep':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:27, about animals brought as offerings.

phrases.english: to leave out the mixed animal,
'or a goat': to leave out a look-alike!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that או includes כלאים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא reads או in the קדשים פסוק as leaving out כלאים, the opposite of including it.

steps.title: What 'or' does depends on which animals the verse lists
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that each פסוק is read by its own setting. In the theft פסוק, ox and sheep cannot produce כלאים, so או includes it. In the קדשים פסוק, sheep and goat can produce כלאים, so או leaves it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: here we learn from the setting of the פסוק, and there we learn from the setting of the פסוק. Here, about theft, the פסוק says 'ox or שה'. You cannot produce כלאים from those two, so 'או' includes כלאים. About קדשים, the פסוק says 'sheep and goat'. You can produce כלאים from those two, so 'או' comes to leave it out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. The word 'or' does not have one fixed job; its job depends on the animals listed next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox and a sheep cannot have offspring together. So in the theft פסוק, a mixed animal could never come from the pair that is listed, and the 'or' must be adding it in. A sheep and a goat can have offspring together, so in the offerings פסוק the 'or' separates them and leaves out the mixed animal.

keyTerms.meaning: From the setting (context) of the פסוק
Theft
Animals set aside as offerings
To leave out, to limit

steps.whatToRemember: The same word או can include or exclude. In the theft פסוק (ox or sheep, a pair that cannot produce כלאים) it includes כלאים, so a thief pays four or five for one. In the קדשים פסוק (sheep and goat, a pair that can) it leaves כלאים out.
steps.confusionAlert: In this step, לְהוֹצִיא כִּלְאַיִם means 'to produce' a mixed animal, meaning to breed one. It does not mean 'to leave out' as it did in step 14.

phrases.english: רבא said: Here it is learned from the setting of the verse,
and there it is learned from the setting of the verse.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא גַּבֵּי גְּנֵיבָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״שׁוֹר אוֹ שֶׂה״,
phrases.english: Here, about theft, where it is written: 'An ox or a seh,'

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיא כִּלְאַיִם מִבֵּינֵיהֶם –
phrases.english: from which you cannot produce a mixed animal,
phrases.notes: Here לְהוֹצִיא means to breed. An ox and a sheep can't have young together.

phrases.english: 'or' is to include the mixed animal.
About offerings, where it is written: 'sheep' and 'goat,'
from which you can produce a mixed animal,
'or' is to leave it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָכָא מֵעִנְיָינֵיהּ דִּקְרָא, וְהָכָא מֵעִנְיָינֵיהּ דִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 16 and backs up the answer from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling the two cases apart by the setting of each פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: או should have one fixed meaning, so it cannot include in one פסוק and exclude in another.
steps.terutzMaskana: או includes when the animals listed cannot produce כלאים (theft), and it excludes when they can (קדשים).
